summary: 学习乐器会同时调用多种能力。文章用脑结构、听觉和老年人学习乐器的研究，分别考察早期训练可能留下的影响，以及晚年开始练习的效果。
logic: 检验学琴让人更聪明的说法
观察训练对应的脑部变化
跟踪早年训练与晚年表现
考察老年初学者的变化

paragraphs.brief: 短期音乐课与儿童智商的实验结果
sentences: Are music lessons the way to get smarter?
上音乐课能让人更聪明吗？
That’s what a lot of parents and experts believe: studying an instrument gives children an advantage in the development of their intellectual, perceptual, and cognitive skills.
不少家长和专家都这样想，认为学习乐器能让儿童在智力、感知与认知能力的发展中占优势。
This may, however, turn out to be wishful thinking.
然而，这或许是一厢情愿的想法。

Two highly convincing trials carried out recently have found no evidence to support this idea; the IQs of pre-school children who attended several weeks of music classes as part of these studies did not differ significantly from the IQs of those who had not.
最近进行的两次非常令人信服的试验没有找到支持这一想法的证据；作为这些研究的一部分参加几个星期音乐课的学龄前儿童的智商与没有参加这种学习的儿童的智商没有很大差别。
paragraphs.gist: 家长常认为学乐器能提高智力，但两项对学龄前儿童的试验发现，上了几周音乐课的孩子与未上课者的智商没有显著差异。

paragraphs.brief: 动作协调练习可能带来晚年收益
sentences: But that does not mean that the advantages of learning to play music are limited to expressing yourself, impressing friends, or just having fun.
但这并不意味着学习演奏音乐的好处仅限于表达自己给朋友留下深刻印象或只是玩乐

A growing number of studies show that learning an instrument in childhood can do something perhaps more valuable for the brain: it can provide benefits as we age, in the form of an added defence against memory loss, cognitive decline, and impaired hearing.
越来越多的研究表明，在童年学习一种乐器或许能对大脑起到更有价值的作用：随着我们老化，它可以提供一些好处，其形式是防止记忆丧失、认知衰落和听力受损。
Not only that, you may well get those benefits even if you haven’t picked up your instrument in years, or decide to take up music for the first time in mid-life or beyond.
即使已经多年没碰过乐器，或直到中年乃至更晚才第一次学音乐，你也很可能获得这些益处。

According to neuropsychologist Brenda Hanna- Pladdy of Emory University in Atlanta, the time spent learning and practising specific types of motor control and coordination—each finger on each hand doing something different, and for wind and brass instruments, also using your mouth and breathing—contributes to the brain boost that shows up later in life.
汉娜－普拉迪认为，学乐器要练特定的动作控制与协调，例如两手各指动作不同，吹奏管乐或铜管乐器还得控制口部和呼吸，这些练习时间可能有助于晚年的大脑表现。
paragraphs.gist: 即便智商收益不明，练乐器所需的手指、呼吸等协调训练仍可能在晚年帮助维持记忆、认知和听力，停练多年或成年才学也可能受益。

paragraphs.brief: 脑部结构怎样随音乐训练改变
sentences: You can even map the impact of musical training on the brain itself.
你甚至可以绘制音乐训练对大脑本身的影响图。
In one study, Harvard neurologist Gottfried Schlaug found that the brains of adult professional musicians had a larger volume of grey matter than the brains of non-musicians had.
哈佛大学神经学家戈特弗里德·施劳格在一项研究中发现，成年职业音乐家的脑灰质体积比非音乐家大。
Schlaug and colleagues also found that after 15 months of musical training in early childhood, structural brain changes associated with motor and auditory improvements begin to appear.
Schlaug和同事还发现，在幼儿期接受了15个月的音乐培训之后，与运动和听觉改善有关的结构性大脑变化开始出现。

‘What’s unique about playing an instrument is that it requires a wide array of brain regions and cognitive functions to work together simultaneously, in both the right and left hemispheres of the brain,’ says Alison Balbag of the University of Southern California.
南加州大学的艾莉森·巴尔巴格：“玩乐器的独特之处在于它需要各种各样的大脑区域和认知功能在大脑的右半球和左半球同时工作。”
‘Playing music may be an efficient way to stimulate the brain,’ she says, ‘cutting across a broad swath of its regions and cognitive functions, and with ripple effects through the decades.’
她说：“演奏可能是一种有效的脑部刺激方式，它同时涉及广泛的脑区和认知功能，影响或许会延续数十年。”
paragraphs.gist: 专业乐手灰质体积较大，幼儿训练十五个月后也开始出现与动作和听觉改善相关的脑部变化，学者认为演奏会同时调动两侧大脑的多个区域。

paragraphs.brief: 早学与长期练习的老年认知差异
sentences: More research is showing this might well be the case.
更多的研究表明，情况很可能如此。

In her first study on the subject, Hanna-Pladdy divided 70 healthy adults between the ages of 60 and 83 into three groups: musicians who had studied an instrument for at least ten years, those who had played between one and nine years, and a control group who had never learned an instrument.
汉娜-帕莱迪在第一次关于该主题的研究中将60至83岁的70名健康成年人分成三个组：至少学习了十年的音乐家、玩了一至九年的音乐家和一个从未学过乐器的控制组。
The group who had studied for at least ten years scored the highest when tested in such areas as non-verbal and visuo-spatial memory, naming objects, and taking in and adapting new information.
学过至少十年乐器的一组，在非语言记忆、视觉空间记忆、命名物体、接收并适应新信息等测试中得分最高。

Her follow-up study a year later confirmed those findings and further suggested that starting musical training before the age of nine and keeping at it for ten years or more may yield the greatest benefits.
一年之后，她的后续研究证实了这些调查结果，并进一步提出，在9岁之前开始音乐培训并保持10年或10年以上可以产生最大的效益。
Interestingly, it was the group who had the lowest level of general education which showed the greatest gap in scores between those who had studied an instrument in childhood and those who had not.
有趣的是，在普通教育水平最低的一组人里，小时候学过乐器者和没学过者之间的分数差距反而最大。
Hanna-Pladdy suspects that musical training could have made up for the lack of cognitive stimulation these people had.
Hanna -Pladdy怀疑音乐培训可以弥补这些人缺乏认知刺激。
paragraphs.gist: 在七十名老年人中，习乐至少十年者在多项认知测试中得分最高，后续研究还提示，九岁前开始、坚持十年以上可能最有利。

paragraphs.brief: 早期训练与晚年的语音辨别能力
sentences: Neuroscientist Nina Kraus of Northwestern University in Chicago has found still more positive effects of early musical training.
芝加哥西北大学的神经科学家Nina Kraus发现早期音乐培训的效果更积极。
She measured the electrical activity in the auditory brainstem of adults, aged 55 to 70, as they responded to the synthesised speech syllable ‘da’.
她让五十五至七十岁的成年人听合成语音音节“da”，测量其听觉脑干在反应时的电活动。
Although none of the subjects had played a musical instrument in 40 years, those who had trained the longest—between four and fourteen years—responded the fastest.
所有受试者都已四十年没有演奏过乐器，然而早年训练时间最长（四至十四年）的人反应最快。

‘That’s significant,’ says Kraus, ‘because hearing tends to decline as we age, including the ability to quickly and accurately discern consonants, a skill crucial to understanding and participating in conversation.
克劳斯说：“这一点很重要，因为听力会随年龄增长而下降，包括快速准确分辨辅音的能力，而这种能力对理解和参与对话十分关键。”

If your nervous system is not keeping up with the timing necessary for encoding consonants, you will lose out on the flow and meaning of the conversation, and that can potentially create a downward spiral leading to a sense of social isolation,’ says Kraus.
克劳斯说：“如果神经系统跟不上辨识辅音所需的精确时序，人就可能跟不上对话，听不明白意思，长此以往便可能陷入恶性循环，觉得自己与外界隔绝。”
In addition, the fact that musical training appears to enhance auditory working memory might help reinforce in later life the memory capacity that facilitates verbal interaction.
此外，音乐培训似乎加强了听力工作记忆，这可能有助于在以后的生活中加强促进口头交流的记忆能力。
paragraphs.gist: 四十年不曾演奏的成年人中，早年练习最久者对语音的神经反应最快，这或许有助于老年人分辨辅音、跟上谈话并保持社交。

paragraphs.brief: 晚年初学钢琴也可能改善认知
sentences: In another study at the University of South Florida, assistant professor of music education Jennifer Bugos studied the impact of elementary piano instruction on adults between the ages of 60 and 85.
在南佛罗里达大学的另一项研究中，音乐教育助理教授Jennifer Bugos研究了初等钢琴教学对60至85岁成年人的影响。

After six months, those who had received piano lessons showed more robust gains in memory, verbal fluency, the speed at which they processed information, planning ability, and other cognitive functions compared with those who had not received the lessons.
6个月后，与那些没有学过钢琴的人相比，那些接受过钢琴课的人在记忆、语言流利、处理信息的速度、规划能力和其他认知功能方面都取得了更强有力的成绩。
Bugos believes that playing an instrument has beneficial effects, regardless of how old the person is when he or she begins.
布戈斯认为，玩乐器可以产生有益的效果，不管他(她)何时开始，年龄多大。
‘Musical training contains all the components of a cognitive training programme that sometimes are overlooked,’ she says.
她说：“音乐训练具备认知训练方案的全部要素，其中有些要素平常容易被忽视。”
‘And just as we work out our bodies, we should work out our minds.’
“就像要锻炼身体一样，我们也应该锻炼大脑。”
paragraphs.gist: 六十至八十五岁的初学者经过半年钢琴课，在记忆、语言流畅度和计划能力等方面比未上课者进步更明显，显示晚年开始练习也可能受益。

items.en: Many parents indicate that their children struggle to learn a musical instrument.
items.zh: 许多家长表示，孩子觉得学习乐器很吃力。
items.why: 文章说不少家长相信学乐器有助于孩子发展智力，这反映的是家长对益处的看法，没有涉及他们的孩子学起来是否吃力。

items.en: The findings of the recent research into pre-school children’s IQs are unreliable.
items.zh: 最近对学龄前儿童智商的研究结果是不可靠的。
items.why: 作者把这两项学龄前儿童智商试验称为“很有说服力”。试验没有发现显著差异，并不代表结果不可靠。

items.en: The main reasons people take up an instrument are that they enjoy playing music and being creative.
items.zh: 人们之所以会使用乐器，主要是因为他们乐于演奏音乐和创作。
items.why: 自我表达、使朋友刮目相看和获得乐趣，都被列为学习乐器可能带来的好处。作者没有把它们列为人们开始学习的主要动机。

items.en: Evidence about the long-term advantages of learning an instrument is increasing.
items.zh: 关于学习乐器具有长期益处的证据越来越多。
items.why: 原文说越来越多的研究发现，童年学乐器可能在衰老时对记忆、认知等产生益处，因此有关长期效应的证据正在增多。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: The studies mentioned in the first paragraph
correct: cast doubt on a belief about the effects of taking music lessons.
使人质疑一种关于音乐课效果的普遍看法。

items.en: According to the second paragraph, there may be many benefits to studying music,
items.zh: 根据第二段学习音乐可能有很多好处
correct: even for those who begin learning in adulthood.
甚至在成年时开始学习的人。

items.en: The phrase ‘this might well be the case’ in the fourth paragraph suggests that
items.zh: 第四段中的`情况很可能如此 ' 一语表明：
correct: learning an instrument may have a lasting impact on brain function.
学习乐器可能对脑功能产生持久影响。

items.en: Which aspect of playing an instrument was included in Hanna-Pladdy’s follow-up study but not in her first study?
items.zh: 玩乐器的哪个方面包括在汉娜-帕莱迪的后续研究中，但在她的第一份研究中却没有？
correct: at which age the person began having lessons

items.en: What do Hanna-Pladdy’s studies suggest about people’s general education?
items.zh: 汉娜－普拉迪的研究对人们接受一般教育的情况提出了什么看法？
correct: Studying music compensates for an otherwise limited level of education.
学习音乐可以弥补教育程度的不足。

items.en: Brenda Hanna-Pladdy believes the cognitive benefits of music lessons are a result of
items.zh: 布伦达·汉娜·帕蒂相信音乐课的认知效益是
items.answer: D · acquiring the particular set of physical skills needed to play an instrument.
items.solution: 习得演奏乐器所需的一组特定身体协调技能。

items.en: The research undertaken by Gottfried Schlaug focused on
items.answer: A · comparing the brains of people who had never played an instrument with those who played for a living.
items.solution: 比较未学过乐器者与职业演奏者的大脑。

items.en: According to Alison Balbag, playing an instrument is a unique experience because it involves
items.zh: Alison Balbag说，玩乐器是一种独特的体验，因为它涉及
items.answer: B · activating many different parts of the brain at the same time.
items.solution: 同时激活大脑的许多不同部分。

items.en: Nina Kraus believes there is a link between better hearing in later life and the experience of
items.zh: 尼娜·克劳斯认为，晚年听力较好与先前哪种经历有关？
items.answer: F · having played an instrument for a considerable length of time.
items.solution: 曾经在相当长一段时间内坚持演奏乐器。

items.zh: 珍妮弗·布戈斯的研究涉及什么？
items.answer: C · teaching a group of older people to play an instrument.
items.solution: 教一组老年人演奏乐器。

pairs: A growing number of studies show
even for those who begin learning in adulthood
take up music for the first time in mid-life or beyond
成年后才第一次开始学习音乐
题干用形容词，定位句改用同词根的副词。
points: 文章说不少家长相信学乐器有助于孩子发展智力，这反映的是家长对益处的看法，没有涉及他们的孩子学起来是否吃力。
题干问“涉及Jennifer Bugos的研究”。定位句写到“在南佛罗里达大学的另一项研究中，音乐教育助理教授Jennifer Bugos研究了初等钢琴教学对60至85岁成年人的影响”。
clauses: A growing number of studies show …: it can provide benefits as we age, in the form of an added defence against memory loss, cognitive decline, and impaired hearing.
“that learning an instrument in childhood can do something perhaps more valuable for the brain”补足 show 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 show 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。

In her first study on the subject, Hanna-Pladdy divided 70 healthy adults between the ages of 60 and 83 into three groups: musicians who had studied an instrument for at least ten years, those …, and a control group who had never learned an instrument.
“who had played between one and nine years”修饰前面的 those。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 who 时，回看 those，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Studies show that learning a musical instrument can bring about significant improvements in your brain.
研究表明，学习一种乐器能显著改善大脑的某些功能。
